newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - April 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - April 3.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories Thursday:
* Apple Computer is actively looking for a friendly merger partner, several executives close to the company said.
* CompuServe said it was in talks to be acquired but would not name the suitor. America Online is said to be a bidder but neither company would confirm that.
* The FCC plans to temporarily stop collecting payments on over $10 billion worth of wireless communications licenses which were auctioned last year.
* Waban backed away from a deal with Kmart and Leonard Green Partners, a buyout firm, which would have combined Waban's Homebase stores with Kmart's Builders Square.
* The Dow industrials fell 94.04 points to close at 6,517.01, resuming a downward slide.
* Toyota Motor took legal steps to try and block Republic Industries from buying up its dealerships.
* General Motors said its sales rose 4.1 percent in March compared to the same month last year.
* The FCC reached a general pact to require network-owned or affiliated television stations in the country's 10 largest television markets to begin broadcasting digital programming within two years.
* ShopKo Stores and Phar-Mor called off their planned $1 billion merger but said they would pursue other merger options.
* New factory orders rose in February although the gain was smaller than expected.

* Federal prosecutors said they charged 18 people, mostly Russian immigrants, with securities fraud for using strong-arm sales tactics and issuing false data to boost the share price of an Internet company with no business.
* Digital Equipment announced a management reorganization, naming Bruce Claflin to lead worldwide sales and marketing of its computers.
* The Fed Bank of New York is said to have taken disciplinary action against J.P. Morgan related to financing it provided to Sumitomo Corp's former top copper trader.
* Market Place: Lucent Technologies share price has been firm relative to the broader technology selloff.
* Many stockbrokers have shifted habits towards more money management rather than selling stocks and more advice rather than cold calls.
